html:
SMTO-GWT-0046 — SMTO couldn't record the progress of a file copy

GUID: 41a6fdf5-4302-40e9-aa98-34b2332c6544
Slug: transfer-checkpoint-invalid
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gwt

What happened

  • While copying a file between computers, SMTO couldn't save how far the copy had got, so it stopped. Depending on when it stopped, part or all of the file may already be at the destination.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check whether your action already happened: on the receiving computer, look for the destination file and compare its size with the original. The copy stopped partway, so the file may be missing, partial or already complete.
  2. Don't start a second copy while this Task is still open. Let it finish or stop it first. Two copies of the same file running at once could overwrite each other.
  3. Only if the file is missing or clearly incomplete, ask SMTO in a new message to copy it again. Repeating a copy that already finished could replace a file that is already correct.

What success looks like

  • The destination file has the expected size and contents, or a new copy finishes and the Task reports it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; this usually points to a problem inside SMTO rather than your files. Don't keep repeating the copy until you know what is at the destination.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Transfer Checkpoint.write refused to record progress because the phase was not a known transfer phase, or the run did not hold exactly one invocation receipt for this operation, so the copy could not advance.

What this means

  • Checkpoint writing rejected an unknown phase or could not find exactly one invocation receipt owned by the transfer's run and operation. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • Checkpoint writing rejected an unknown phase or could not find exactly one invocation receipt owned by the transfer's run and operation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the checkpoint phase and matching run, operation and invocation identities; determine whether zero or multiple claims were found.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the native run's receipt rows for this run_id and operation_id: exactly one owned claim must carry the gateway_transfer metadata, and an invalid phase points to a code defect. Find the last recorded transfer phase and inspect the source and destination paths (existence, size, SHA-256) before any new copy; resume only through the owning run, never create an alternate claim or replay a commit.
  • Inspect the existing transfer and ownership receipt. Resume only through its owning task; do not create an alternate claim or replay completed publication.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • One valid owned invocation accepts the supported checkpoint transition without repeating published content.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
